headlines.summary: 돈 버는 법 아끼는 법 자산 대부분 부동산에 몰려 배당형 ETF·IRP 등 활용 땐 금융자산 불리고 복리효과도 은퇴 후엔 이자형 상품 추천 예측 가능한 현금흐름 장점 사진=게티이미지뱅크 Q. 서울 방배동에 거주하는 55세 직장인이다. 배우자는 전업주부고, 자녀는 올해 사회생활을 시작했다. 자산의 대부분이 집에 몰려 있다.

headlines.title: 전세 준 1주택 자 양도세 2배 뛸 수도 …‘ 세입자 밀어내기 ’ 현실화하나
headlines.summary: ■장특공제 축소 개편안 적용해보니 보유·거주기간 최대 40% 반영서 보유 비중 줄이고 거주 비중 확대 10년 보유·3년 거주자 기준으로 공제율 반토막…稅부담 크게 늘어 서울 시내 한 아파트 단지의 모습. 연합뉴스 이재명 대통령이 24일 장기보유특별공제 개편 방향에 대한 사실상의 가이드라인을 제시하면서 부동산 시장에서 파장이 예고되고 있다.

headlines.title: 李 "오래 투자했다고 양도세 깎아주면 투기 권장… 실거주 감면 은 필요"

headlines.title: 유가 나흘째 급등 105달러 … 국내 경유 2000원 넘어
headlines.summary: 美-이란 휴전 이전 수준으로 복귀 서울의 한 주유소에 기름 가격이 적혀 있다. 뉴스1 호르무즈 해협에서 미국과 이란의 군사적 긴장감이 높아지면서 국제 유가가 다시 오름세를 보이고 있다. 중동 리스크가 재부각되면서 글로벌 원유 시장이 ‘휴전 이전’ 수준으로 되돌아가는 분위기다.

headlines.title: 석유 최고가격의 그림자 …주유소 83곳 2주째 휴업

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Koo Emphasizes Promoting Regional Consumption and Boosting Domestic Demand
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul visited the Bucheon Walking Festival and met with major corporate leaders, emphasizing efforts to promote regional consumption, improve small business conditions, and encourage innovation for discovering the next semiconductor industry.

key_headlines.title: Korea's Q1 GDP Surprises with 1.7% Growth, Nearly Double Initial Forecast
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's first quarter GDP growth reached 1.7% quarter-on-quarter, significantly exceeding the Bank of Korea's February forecast of 0.9%, marking the strongest growth in over five years and pushing analysts to revise upward full-year growth expectations.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Hits Record High for Fourth Consecutive Day Amid Global Market Optimism
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index reached new all-time highs for four consecutive trading days, with individual investors actively buying KOSPI-tracking ETFs while reducing KOSDAQ holdings, as global central banks prepare for policy announcements next week.

key_headlines.title: New Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song Takes Office Amid Rate Decision Expectations
key_headlines.summary: New BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song assumed office with attention focused on the May monetary policy committee meeting, as uncertainty grows from international tensions and semiconductor market variables affecting Korea's 2% growth target.

key_headlines.title: Korea-Vietnam Science and Technology Innovation Forum Strengthens AI, Semiconductor, and Bio Collaboration
key_headlines.summary: South Korea and Vietnam launched a joint science and technology innovation forum during President Lee's state visit, committing to enhanced cooperation in AI, semiconductors, secondary batteries, biotechnology, and energy sectors.

sections.Hot Economy News: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul is actively engaging with both small business operators and major corporate leaders to stimulate domestic demand and encourage innovation. He visited the Bucheon Walking Festival to encourage regional consumption and met with Samsung and SK Hynix executives, urging them to pursue innovation beyond the current semiconductor achievements. The government is demonstrating comprehensive support for both small and large enterprises through targeted fiscal measures and policy coordination.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's economy delivered a surprising Q1 performance with 1.7% growth, nearly double the Bank of Korea's initial 0.9% forecast, prompting analysts to revise 2026 full-year growth expectations upward to potentially 2.4-3%. New BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song faces immediate pressure as the May monetary policy committee meeting draws attention amid international tensions and semiconductor uncertainties. Global central banks are also adjusting policies, with the Philippines raising its base rate despite economic slowdown concerns as war-driven commodity prices fuel inflation pressures.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI index achieved its fourth consecutive all-time high, reflecting strong market sentiment, while KOSDAQ reached the 1,200 level for the first time in 25 years. Individual investors are actively purchasing KOSPI-tracking ETFs but reducing KOSDAQ holdings, indicating selective market positioning. Global markets showed mixed results with S&P 500 and NASDAQ reaching record highs on US-Iran renegotiation hopes, while the won-dollar exchange rate continued appreciating for the fourth consecutive day due to Middle East tensions.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea is strengthening international technology partnerships, particularly through the Korea-Vietnam Science and Technology Innovation Forum focusing on AI, semiconductors, secondary batteries, biotechnology, and energy collaboration. Domestic stock markets showed notable strength in power equipment, semiconductor, and shipbuilding sectors, with multiple companies reaching new highs. In the global battery market, Chinese leaders CATL and BYD are competing intensely on technology, with CATL emphasizing rapid charging capabilities while BYD highlights mass production readiness.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices have risen for 62 consecutive weeks amid supply constraints and renewed speculation concerns, while the jeonse (deposit rental) market is simultaneously experiencing sharp price increases. Policy debates intensified around apartment lottery qualifications and redevelopment projects, with former Land Minister Byun Chang-heum arguing that private redevelopment is driving up overall housing prices rather than providing affordable solutions. The government is facing pressure to implement more inclusive housing policies beyond traditional redevelopment approaches.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Department of Justice discontinued its investigation into Federal Reserve Chairman Powell, removing political pressure related to interest rate policy as his term approaches May expiration. Global markets responded positively to hopes of US-Iran renegotiations, though tensions persist with the U.S. deploying additional naval assets while Iran reportedly increases mine deployment in the Strait of Hormuz. Next week's key events include FOMC, ECB, and BOJ meetings where investors will seek guidance on rate decisions and the Fed's future leadership.
sections.AI & Economy: China is strengthening AI investment restrictions against U.S. companies amid intensifying technology competition, mirroring U.S. sanctions on Chinese AI and semiconductor investments. Anthropic's survey of 81,000 Claude users revealed that increased AI adoption paradoxically heightens job security anxiety among workers despite productivity gains, raising concerns about workforce displacement. Korean companies are expanding AI-related international partnerships, with ventures like Han-Mi Global and Naver Cloud targeting global data center markets in Saudi Arabia and other regions.
sections.Others: Contrarian investor Michael Burry is buying Microsoft and Adobe stocks, reversing his previous AI skepticism amid software replacement concerns, though his track record shows mixed results. The government's suggestion to restructure education funding allocations has sparked unified opposition from education authorities across all 17 provinces, threatening to become a major budget battle. KB Kookmin Bank upgraded its non-face-to-face retirement pension service, improving user convenience through enhanced digital platforms and professional fund consulting partnerships.
